window.standing: Born as the third step of the code spine (base -> base pair -> tester), the first real device — the system's notary that runs a proof as a subprocess and produces an eight-field VALIDATION whose verdict comes from the subject's exit code, not granted.

Same day grew its other half — the kernel-owned network's MEASURED seal (isolation.py) — completing the 'tester + kernel-owned network' spine step's no-route half; proven green with no install, the hollow-tester and hollow-seal killers verified by falsification.

Open edge (a) closed — VALIDATIONS are now PERSISTED to beside-code git-JSON (validation_store.py: a validations/<stem>.json beside the proofs each seals, Law 5), NOT db_domain; run_proof still writes nothing and the append-only store refuses a drifted record.

PROVED — THE QUORUM SIGNATURE GATE HAS AN ADDRESS. A node proved by human judgment can now actually be sealed. node_classes/concept-piece.json specified this gate on 2026-07-15 and ZERO concept-piece VALIDATIONs existed in the ten days since — not because a reviewer was slow, but because validations_path_for derived a seal's address from a PROOF FILE path and a concept-piece has no proof file, so the single write-door could not physically accept the record. The gate was never awaiting a signature; it was awaiting an ADDRESS, and CC repeatedly reported the former, which is what kept it stuck. Closed with validations_path_for_artifact (the seal lands beside the artifact, derived not chosen, Law 5) and cairn/tester/quorum.py. Same ratified eight fields, same persist_validation, no rival door (Law 6) — only the addressing was ever missing. Physics: a notary who also reviewed is REFUSED (verdict and seal are different hands; a self-seal is the hollow build, Law 8), a signature with no restated-back understanding is REFUSED (a rubber stamp proves someone clicked, not that anyone read), a quorum means DISTINCT hands, and a rejection is a recorded RED that kicks back (CP2), not an exception. Proven 9/9; full suite 32/32 green, run twice.
